children: CIMB could have compelling growth opportunities from converting deposits held by its affluent customers into investment products, offering its own investment products and expanding cross-border wealth services, Hong Leong IB analyst Raymond Ng says in a note. The lender targets wealth assets under management of 600 billion-650 billion ringgit and revenue of 5 billion-6 billion ringgit by 2030, potentially contributing 60-80 basis points toward its 13%-14% ROE target, he notes. He remains positive on CIMB's move toward capital-light income, although the risk of deposit outflows and challenges in executing its strategy could limit near-term earnings growth. Hong Leong maintains a hold rating on CIMB and keeps target price at 7.70 ringgit. Shares are 0.4% lower at 7.05 ringgit. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
